newsitem.title: USA: Cornerstone in $1.06 billion property deal - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Cornerstone in $1.06 billion property deal - WSJ.

text.p: Cornerstone Properties Inc has agred to buy 11 downtown properties in six U.S. cities from a Dutch pension fund for $1.06 billion in stock and cash, the Wall Street Journal said Monday.
Under terms of the deal, Cornerstone will pay $508 million in cash and $547 million in stock to Atlanta-based Dutch Institutional Holding Co. -- part of one of the Netherland's biggest pensions.
The pension will also loan Cornerstone $250 million, to be paid back over 10 years, the paper said.
The porfolio includes two buildings in Atlanta, three in Alexandria, Virginia, two in Boston, two in Washington, one in Charlotte, North Carolina, and one in Chicago, the paper said.
After the deal Dutch Institutional will hold 40 percent of Cornerstone's stock and fill two seats on Cornerstone's 12-member board, the newspaper added.
